flags.summary: A manager reviewed a full call with a 52-year-old diabetic prospect who disclosed multiple active injuries and pain during kettlebell movements, and every coaching note concerned sales technique; neither participant raised clinical screening or clearance at any point.
evidence: I'm diabetic, so I have the co-sensor, I fast, I literally just had my breakfast or lunch.

at the moment I've got loads of injuries, loads of little needles, so forearms, shoulder, rear delto on this side. If I'm having a shower, for example, I've got to be very careful how I stretch, I can't do that, it's very painful.

in the past when I've done deadlifts, I've just stopped doing deadlifts now, I certainly stopped doing squats years ago... weighted squats with significant weight I just don't do anymore, not for years and years.
when I tried to clean and press, for example, I noticed there was some pain here, it really put me off.
mindful I don't want to make things worse, because I can easily make things worse, so I really don't want to do that.

flags.summary: Rep characterised a prospect by perceived sexual orientation and the manager restated it explicitly rather than correcting it.
evidence: And then the other guy I had, he seemed a little bit zesty, that's for sure.
Zesty? You're saying he seemed zesty? I don't even know what to do with that. Oh, you mean gay?

flags.summary: Manager coached the rep to withhold a favourable assessment of a prospect's nutrition, on the stated grounds that affirming it makes the nutrition pillar harder to sell.
evidence: Again, you want to withhold comments about if their diet being good or anything like that. You want to stay neutral.
And because of earlier you told him his diet is good, the nutrition part is going to be tough for you to land now.
But it also devalues it because now he's trying to sell you on like, well, I actually do need more nutrition help versus you saying, look, your nutrition is not quite where it needs to be.

flags.summary: Deposit amounts referenced inside the business vary by an order of magnitude with no stated standard — the manager cites $1,000 deposits as routine while the same rep presented $100 and $200 as the customary figure to prospects the previous day.
evidence: I've had people that put down $1,000 deposits and told me for sure next week, they're going to come in and they're going to get this credit card and they ghost me even with the $1,000 deposit, they ghost me.
He was talking to you about payments. was trying to figure things out with the credit union.
I did like the Tyler guy. I was like, yeah, he's gonna come in last Thursday, almost no responses.

flags.summary: The reviewed prospect explicitly challenged the claim that kettlebells eliminate pain, and the coaching addressed only how to reframe his scepticism, never whether the claim is substantiated.
evidence: Again, it's quite a big claim. I've noticed that you're saying kettlebells will eliminate, but if I read one of the areas it will actually help or eliminate these small pains. I'm going to try, but I'm also mindful of...

I wouldn't even hold the word skeptical. I would say, well, it sounds like you're obviously doing the research, so you're definitely informing yourself, and it's awesome that you're in a place where you're willing to give it a shot. What is it that makes you feel like, from what you've seen, that you are willing to give it a shot? So then he has to sell.
